questions.question: Which of the following is the main percussion instrument used in the performance of the Mohiniyattam dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Edakka**__.

__
 
• The musical instruments usually used in Mohiniyattam are **Mridangam** or Madhalam (barrel drum), Idakka (hourglass drum), flute, Veena, and Kuzhitalam (cymbals).
 
• Mohiniyattam is based on **Natya Shastra’s lasya style**.
 
• Mohiniyattam is one of the classical dance forms that originated in** Kerala**, the other one being **Kathakali**.
 
• Mohiniyattam gets its name from the word "**Mohini**", the feminine form of **Lord Vishnu**, the word means dance of Mohini.
 
• The dance has a major **emphasis on facial expressions and hand gestures**.
 
• **Dr. Sunanda Nair** became the first in India to acquire a Master's degree in Mohiniyattam.
 
• Notable dancers of Mohiniyattam are** Sunanda Nair, Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, Jayaprabha Menon, Pallavi Krishnan, Gopika Varma, Vijayalakshmi, Radha Dutta, Rema Shrikant**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f9b470bc27066ddaa89ce0f7305c276140567445bd24a847caca3180aa37e0e8.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Musical instruments used in Kathak dance are Esraj, Bansuri, Ghungharu, Harmonium, Santur, Pakhawaj, Sarod, Tabla, **Sitar**, Tanpura, etc.
 
• The instruments used in **Odissi** dance include tabla, pakhavaj, harmonium, swarmandal, **sitar**, flute, violin, and cymbals.
 
• **Dharma **is a traditional percussion instrument with a rich bass sound essential for Chau's dance performance. Chau dance is majorly known in Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal.
 
• Nagada is mainly used in the Geedad dance form.

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT an Odissi dancer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anita Ratnam**__

__
 
• **Anita Ratnam** is primarily known for her work in Bharatanatyam, Mohiniyattam, and Kathakali, not Odissi.
 
• **Kumkum Mohanty**, **Sonal Mansingh**, and **Protima Bedi** are all well-known Odissi dancers.
 
• Odissi is one of the classical dance forms of India, which originated in the state of Odisha.
 
• Odissi dance is characterized by its fluid movements, sculpturesque poses, and intricate footwork.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Odissi dance is known for its grace, elegance, and expressive gestures, which are deeply rooted in the devotional practices of the region.
 
• Contemporary practitioners of Odissi continue to innovate while preserving the rich heritage of the dance form.

questions.question: Who among the following Padma Vibhushan awardees belongs to Kalka-Bindadin gharana of Kathak?

__
 
• **Brijmohan Mishra, popularly known as Birju Maharaj**, belongs to the Kalka-Bindadin gharana of Kathak.
 
• He is a recipient of the **Padma Vibhushan**, India's second-highest civilian award.
 
• Birju Maharaj is renowned for his contributions to the classical dance form of **Kathak**.
 
• He has also been honored with numerous other awards, including the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and the Kalidas Samman.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance and traces its origins to the nomadic bards of ancient northern India, known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• The **Kalka-Bindadin gharana** is one of the three main gharanas (schools) of Kathak, known for its intricate footwork and expressive gestures.
 
• Birju Maharaj has been instrumental in popularizing Kathak across the globe and has trained several generations of dancers.
 
• His family has been associated with Kathak for several generations, making significant contributions to the art form.

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms traces its lineage to the ancient dance of Sadir Attam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam, **a classical dance form from **Tamil Nadu,** traces its roots to the ancient dance known as **Sadir Attam.**
 
• Originally called** Sadir or Dasi Attam**, Bharatanatyam evolved from the** temple dance tradition of Sadir Attam.**
 
• **E Krishna Iyer and Rukmini Devi Arundale **played key roles in transforming Sadir into Bharatanatyam, particularly by refining the Pandanallur style of dance.
 
• The name Bharatanatyam translates to "the pure form." Historically, Sadir Attam was performed by Devadasis, meaning "Servants of God." However, in modern Tamil, the term "Devar-Adiyar" is often used derogatorily, equating it with "prostitute."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form from India, originating in Tamil Nadu, and recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi. It showcases religious themes and spiritual ideas, particularly from Shaivism, Hinduism, and Jainism.
 
• **Kuchipudi **is a dance-drama performance originating from the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh, India. It is one of the eight major classical dances of India, acknowledged by the Sangeet Natak Akademi and the Ministry of Culture.
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is an Indian classical dance form originating from the state of Kerala.
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical Indian dance-drama form with a history spanning 300 years, originating in Kerala in the 17th century.

questions.question: Gobinda Chandra Pal is an awardee of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award for the year 2022. He contributed to the field of:

The correct answer is __**Odissi Dance (Gotipua)**__

__
 
• **Gobinda Chandra Pal** is an awardee of the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award** for the year **2022**.
 
• He has made significant contributions to the field of **Odissi Dance (Gotipua)**.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award is a prestigious recognition given to individuals for their outstanding contributions to Indian performing arts.
 
• **Odissi Dance** is one of the classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha.
 
• **Gotipua** is a traditional dance form from Odisha, where young boys dress up as women to perform the dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi** is India's national academy for music, dance, and drama. It was established in **1952** by the Government of India.
 
• The Akademi's primary objectives include the promotion and preservation of the performing arts in India.
 
• In addition to the Amrit Award, the Sangeet Natak Akademi also confers other awards such as the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar, and the Tagore Ratna.
 
• The **Gotipua** dance tradition has been a significant part of the Odissi dance heritage and has influenced the classical dance form of Odissi.

questions.question: Indian Classical Dance is an umbrella under which various performing arts whose theory and practice can be traced to the Sanskrit text, Natya-Shastra, the foundational treatise by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharata Muni**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharata Muni** is the author of the Natya-Shastra, the foundational treatise on Indian classical dance and performing arts.
 
• The Natya-Shastra is a comprehensive text that covers various aspects of performing arts, including dance, music, and theater.
 
• It is considered one of the oldest and most authoritative texts on classical Indian dance and drama.
 
• The treatise lays down the principles and techniques that form the basis of various Indian classical dance forms such as Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, and others.
 
• Bharata Muni's work has had a profound influence on the development and preservation of Indian performing arts over centuries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Natya-Shastra** is believed to have been written between 200 BCE and 200 CE.
 
• The text is divided into 36 chapters and contains around 6000 verses.
 
• It covers a wide range of topics, including the structure of a play, the types of drama, the principles of stage design, and the techniques of acting and dance.
 
• The Natya-Shastra also discusses the role of the audience and the impact of the performance on the viewers.
 
• Bharata Muni's work continues to be a vital source of knowledge for scholars, performers, and enthusiasts of Indian classical arts.

questions.question: Bharatanatyam is traditionally performed to which type of music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carnatic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is traditionally performed in **Carnatic music**.
 
• **Carnatic music** is a** classical music** tradition originating from** South India**.
 
• It features **intricate melodies**,** rhythmic patterns**, and **compositions **in languages like **Telugu, Tamil, and Sanskrit**.
 
• **Bharatanatyam dancers **synchronize their movements with the rhythm and melody of **Carnatic music** during performances.
 
• **Bharatanatyam**, a **classical dance **form from** Tamil Nadu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baul**

 
 
• **Baul **is a **spiritual and musical tradition** from **Bengal**.
 
• It explores themes of **love, devotion, and spiritual enlightenment**.
 
• Typically accompanied by **instruments** like **ektara, dotara, and khamak**.
 
 
 
• **Hindustani**
 
 
• **Hindustani music **is the** classical music** tradition of **North India**.
 
• It features **rich melodies**, **intricate rhythms**, and** improvisation**.
 
• Common instruments include **sitar, tabla**, **sarangi**, and **flute**.
 
 
 
• **Lavani**
 
 
• **Lavani** is a traditional **dance and musical** **form** from **Maharashtra**, **India**.
 
• Known for its **energetic movements**,** rhythmic footwork**, and **expressive storytelling**.
 
• **Lavani **often explores themes of l**ove, romance, and social issues**.

questions.question: Bhutia dance is performed in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhutia dance:-**

 
 
• **It is an integral part of Bhutia culture, traditionally performed during festivals, celebrations, and community gatherings. **
 
• These vibrant dances showcase the rich heritage and storytelling traditions of the Bhutia people, an indigenous group inhabiting the Himalayan regions of India, Nepal, and Bhutan.
 
• **In India, it is performed in Sikkim.**
 
• Bhutia dances are characterized by their energetic movements, colorful costumes, and lively music. Some of the most popular Bhutia dances include:
 
 
• **Denzong-Neh-Na**: This lively dance is performed by both men and women and mimics the movements of birds in flight.
 
• **Ta-Shi-Yang-Ku**: This graceful dance is performed by women and depicts the movements of swans gliding across a lake.
 
• **Tashi Shabdo:** This energetic dance is performed by men and showcases their strength and agility.
 
 
 
• Bhutia dance costumes are elaborate and colorful, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of the Bhutia people. Men typically wear long robes and hats, while women wear colorful dresses and jewelry.
 
• The music for Bhutia dances is traditionally played on instruments such as drums, flutes, and cymbals. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **West Bengal:-**

 
 
• **It is a state in eastern India known for its rich cultural heritage, vibrant festivals, and stunning natural beauty. **
 
• The state's capital is Kolkata, formerly known as Calcutta, which is a major commercial and cultural hub.
 
• West Bengal is famous for its exquisite handicrafts, delicious cuisine, and renowned literary figures.
 
• The state is also home to the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Odisha:-**
 
 
• **It is a state in eastern India known for its ancient temples, breathtaking beaches, and vibrant tribal culture. **
 
• The state's capital is Bhubaneswar, which is known as the "Temple City of India" for its numerous ancient temples.
 
• Odisha is also famous for its rich handloom tradition, exquisite handicrafts, and delicious cuisine.
 
• The state is home to the Lingaraj Temple, one of the largest temples in India, and the Konark Sun Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Nagaland:-**
 
 
• **It is a state in northeastern India known for its lush green hills, colorful festivals, and unique tribal culture. **
 
• The state's capital is Kohima, which is known as the "Land of the Nagas". Nagaland is famous for its rich biodiversity, vibrant festivals, and traditional crafts.
 
• The state is home to the Naga people, who are divided into numerous tribes, each with its own distinct culture, language, and traditions.

questions.question: Alarmel Valli is an Indian classical dancer and choreographer and a foremost exponent of the ______ dance form of Bharatanatyam.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandanallur style**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alarmel Valli **is an Indian classical dancer and choreographer and a foremost exponent of the **Pandanallur style** dance form of **Bharatanatyam**. 
 
• She established The Dipasikha Dance Foundation in Chennai in 1984, where she imparts training in Bharatanatyam.
 
• In 1991, Alarmel Valli became the second youngest dancer to receive the Padma Shri from the Government of India, following Vyjayanthimala.
 
• She was honored with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2001 by India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama.
 
• This was followed by the Padma Bhushan award from the Government of India in 2004 and the Chevalier of Arts and Letters award from the Government of France, also in 2004.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Pandanallur style** of Bharatanatyam, a prominent form of Indian classical dance, originated in the village of Pandanallur in the Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu.
 
• It was developed by the renowned dance guru Meenakshi Sundaram Pillai (1869–1964).
 
• This style is esteemed for its intricate choreography, including the renowned Nine or Ten Tanjore Quartet pada-varnams.
 
• Pillai, credited with the choreography of these masterpieces, introduced distinctive hand gestures known as "hands" and also crafted the adavu choreography for the swara passages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tarangam **is a distinctive feature of Kuchipudi, a traditional dance-drama from Andhra Pradesh, often serving as the concluding act of a performance.
 
• **Vazhuvoor, also known as Vizhuvur, **stands as one of the foundational styles of Bharatanatyam, a prominent Indian classical dance form.
 
• **The Melattur style** of Bharatanatyam emerged as a refinement of the devadasi tradition, showcasing its evolution and adaptation over time.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dances is referred to as the dance of the storytellers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

__
 
• **Kathak **is one of the classical dances of India.
 
• Kathak dance originated from **Uttar Pradesh (U.P)** in North India.
 
• It was **primarily a temple or village performance wherein the dancers narrated stories from ancient scriptures**.
 
• Usually a solo performance, the **dancer often pauses to recite verses **followed by their execution through movement.
 
• Kathak is the only form of classical dance that belongs to North Indian music.
 
• The foundations of Kathak are rooted in **Natya Shastra**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b0ad56825d694bd7dd609d9c597208d85b4a4129944d7a06a17e33eb37ad93e.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi:**

 
 
• **​**Odissi is similar to Bharatnatyam in the mudras and posture to express emotions.
 
• During h Odissi dance the lower body remains static and there is movement in the torso.
 
• Odissi is also known as a **mobile sculpture**.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**:
 
 
• It is a classical dance of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• Kuchipudi derives its name from the village Kusselevapuri in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• **Vijaynagar and Golcando's** rulers patronized the dance form.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali**:
 
 
• It is the most difficult style of the traditional dance form in which actors speak sign language and hand gestures are used to dictate words.
 
• Kathakali is based on the epics of **Ramayana and Mahabharata**.

questions.question: The masculine aspect of the Manipuri classical dance is known as:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following classical dance forms is usually concluded with Tarangam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical dance form from the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The dance is known for its graceful movements and strong narrative/dramatic character.
 
• **Tarangam** is a distinctive feature of Kuchipudi, typically performed towards the end of the dance recital.
 
• During Tarangam, dancers often balance on the edges of a brass plate while executing intricate footwork.
 
• This performance showcases the dancer's control, skill, and ability to maintain balance while performing complex movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi** has its roots in the ancient Hindu Sanskrit text **Natyashastra**, which is considered the foundation of Indian classical dance forms.
 
• The dance form traditionally narrates stories from Hindu epics and mythology, such as the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
